FAQs for Students

Everything you need to know about learning English, French, or German with us.

Home / FAQs for Students
Volunteering or teaching with us instead? Visit our FAQs for Teachers.

34 questions across 6 themes

01

Joining & Eligibility

Who can apply, what it costs, and what level you need to start.

Our programme is for Palestinian students based in Gaza, the West Bank, or displaced elsewhere because of the war. Students are primarily aged 13–30, though every application is considered individually.

No. Every lesson is completely free, always. There is no cost to you at any stage, for as long as you keep learning with us.

You can learn English, French, or German with a volunteer educator matched to your goals and schedule.

Any level. Whether you are a complete beginner or already advanced, we assess your level during the application process and match you accurately before lessons begin.

No, you can apply on your own — a parent or guardian’s permission is not required. Our safeguarding policy still applies to every student, whatever your age.

02

Applying & Getting Matched

How the application works, and how we pair you with an educator.

Three formats, and we match you to the one that fits your circumstances: small group lessons (our default, learning alongside a couple of other students), one-to-one lessons (reserved for exam preparation or students with special educational needs), and fully asynchronous lessons for students without reliable internet for live classes.

Applying only takes a few minutes: tell us your language, level, and availability. Applications open twice a year, about a month before each term begins, and matching happens once applications close for that term.

If student enrolment is closed, you can join the waiting list to be notified as soon as it reopens ahead of the next term — we also announce reopening dates on our website and social media. In the meantime, you are welcome to explore our free resources, including recommended YouTube channels and language-learning materials.

We match you with a volunteer educator based on your language, level, and availability, so lessons fit your goals and schedule.

Our volunteer educators come from more than 15 countries, and all are trained to support students learning under difficult circumstances.

Yes. If you would feel more comfortable with a same-gender educator, let us know in your application and we will take this into account when matching you.

Yes. Volunteers who teach students who are minors are required to provide a valid, current background check before they begin teaching, alongside safeguarding training and a signed volunteer agreement.

03

Lessons & Groups

How long the programme runs, group sizes, scheduling, and staying in touch.

Each term lasts a minimum of three months. You are welcome to keep learning with us beyond your first term, for as long as it is helpful to you.

No. Sessions are set at 60 or 90 minutes a week to keep the programme sustainable for our volunteer educators, so we are not able to offer additional weekly lesson time.

Small groups usually have three or four other students learning alongside you, at a similar level.

Yes. If you would like to learn alongside a sibling or other family member, mention this in your application or contact us, and we will try to place you together where possible.

Mini-groups keep the same overall topic for everyone but let your teacher adjust the level of support and challenge for each student, using activities like debates, role-plays, and collaborative tasks to keep everyone engaged. It is a format that works well: it builds peer support and conversation practice while keeping lessons personalised to your level.

No. Each student or mini-group is matched with one volunteer educator at a time, so your teacher can build a consistent picture of your progress and needs.

There are no fixed lesson times. Teachers and students are matched by availability, and sessions usually happen in the morning, in the afternoon, or at weekends — we generally avoid evenings or nights, which can be difficult for students in Gaza.

Live lessons are typically held over Google Meet, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp is used for day-to-day communication, since it is the most widely used messaging tool in Palestine.

04

Progress, Materials & Certificates

Tracking your learning, exam preparation, and what you receive along the way.

Your teacher records your progress using a dedicated tracking resource throughout the term, so both you and your teacher can see how your learning is developing.

Your portfolio is completed at the end of the term: a short written essay and a recorded audio piece, which we use to check your level.

Completing your portfolio and assessments is what allows us to confirm your progress. If it is not completed, we will not be able to issue a certificate or confirm a new level for you at the end of the term.

Yes. Certificates are provided to students who complete their term’s requirements, including their portfolio and assessments.

Yes. If you are preparing for an official exam such as IELTS, TOEFL, DELF, DALF, or a Goethe-Institut exam, you can be matched for one-to-one lessons with focused coaching and practice tests, available from Intermediate (B1) level upward.

Yes. Every student receives a textbook and a curated collection of learning resources, matched to your level and goals.

Yes — if your teacher is also continuing to volunteer with us, you can usually continue learning together into the next term.

05

Changes & Rematching

What to do if something changes, and how rematching works.

We consider a rematch when there is a genuine, ongoing difficulty — for example, a serious scheduling conflict, an unresponsive teacher, or a mismatch in teaching style that has not improved despite raising it with us. We cannot guarantee a rematch based on personal preferences unrelated to your learning.

Let us know, and you will continue lessons with the rest of your group. We will try to add another student to the group where possible, especially if this happens near the start of the term.

First, try reaching out again directly. If you still do not hear back, or this keeps happening, contact us and we will follow up with your teacher and arrange another match if needed.

Your teacher will continue your learning asynchronously — sending structured lesson activities or planned questions through your usual messaging platform — so a technical problem does not disrupt your progress.

We ask you to attend your sessions consistently, let your teacher (or us) know as early as possible if you need to reschedule, and complete the assessments and portfolio work used to track your progress. Being an active, engaged partner in your own lessons helps your teacher help you.

Three months is the minimum term length, and if you need to stop after that, that is completely fine. You are welcome to apply again in a future term when applications reopen.

06

Safety & Support

What to do if something does not feel right.

Tell us right away by emailing safeguarding@ramzunalanguages.org. You will be taken seriously, your concern will be handled confidentially by our safeguarding lead, and you will never be in trouble for speaking up.

No matching questions found.

Try a broader term such as “lessons”, “certificate”, or “apply”.

Still have questions?

Our coordination team is happy to walk you through the details.
